inputs.original_text: Tensions in Nigeria’s health sector escalated on Thursday as workers under the Joint Health Sector Unions and the Assembly of Healthcare Professional Associations took to the streets in Abuja, protesting controversial reform bills currently before the National Assembly. The demonstrators gathered at the Unity Fountain in Maitama, voicing strong opposition to the proposed legislation, which [...] The post Health sector tensions boil over as workers protest reform bills in Abuja appeared first on Latest Nigeria News | Top Stories from Ripples Nigeria .
inputs.modified_text: Health workers from the Joint Health Sector Unions and the Assembly of Healthcare Professional Associations protested at Unity Fountain in Maitama, Abuja, on Thursday over reform bills before the National Assembly. Frontline workers deserve a hearing, but their warning shouldn’t become a veto over reforms. The responsibility to weigh competing interests and make policy belongs to lawmakers, accountable to the public—not to any union protecting its place in the system. Patients need a health service that works, and preserving the status quo is not automatically the same as protecting them. The bills should be judged on whether they serve families and the public good, not simply on whether organised groups approve.
